ai.stableNodeKey: (outline) § subtitle#0

content.text: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green.¹ One of them serves all live traffic while the other sits idle; you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step.² Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch.³ The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release, which is why the idle environment is scaled down between releases.⁴

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#0

content.text:
¹ These environments are identical to ensure consistency.
 ² This allows for zero-downtime deployments and easy rollback.
 ³ This is a key benefit of blue-green deployments, enabling rapid recovery from issues.
 ⁴ Scaling down helps manage costs, but the infrastructure still incurs some expense.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#1

snapshot.content: Database migrations must be backward compatible

content.text: Database migrations must be backward compatible, allowing the old version to function with the new schema. Both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration. If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; instead, split the migration into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#2

snapshot.content: Access to load balancer listener rules is essential

content.text: You need access to the load balancer's listener rules, as the switch involves changing which target group the listener forwards to.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#3

content.text: A dashboard or query showing the 5xx error rate per environment is needed to differentiate errors between green and blue environments.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#4

content.text: Deploy version
to
orders-green
using the same build artifact that passed staging. All green instances should report the new version, and blue should still serve 100% of traffic.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#0

content.text: Apply database migrations from the new release once, from a single job. The migration job should exit with code 0, and blue should continue serving requests without new errors, confirming backward compatibility.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#1

content.text: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all return
. If any instance fails health checks after 10 minutes, stop and roll back by tearing down green, leaving blue to serve traffic.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#2

content.text: Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. All smoke tests must pass. If one fails, treat it as a failed health check and stop.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#3
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § code#0

content.text: Within about 30 seconds, new requests should be served by green, and blue should receive no new connections.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#4

content.text: Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes. If the error rate rises above 2% at any point, switch back to blue using
$BLUE_TG_ARN
(traffic returns to blue within about 30 seconds). If it stays at or below 2%, continue.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#5

content.text: Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours as a rollback target.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#6

content.text: After 24 hours without a switch-back, scale blue down. Blue then becomes the idle environment for the next release, with roles reversed.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#7

content.text: Blue is live, and green is idle.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#8

content.text: The process includes explicit rollback points if health checks or smoke tests fail, or if the error rate on green exceeds 2% after traffic switch. These ensure customer impact is minimized.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#9

content.text: The new version is deployed to green, traffic is switched, and blue is retired after a 24-hour standby period, becoming the idle environment for the next release.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#10

content.text: Rolling back before step 5 is inexpensive as customers haven't seen the new version yet.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#0

content.text: Switching back after step 5 is quick, but in-flight requests might fail and require client retries.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#1

content.text: Neither rollback method reverts the database, emphasizing the importance of backward-compatible migrations.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#2

content.text: Always record what caused a failure before retrying, as the same build often fails for the same reason.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#3

content.text: Do not run the next release's database migrations while the blue environment is on standby.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#4

content.text: Running migrations on standby can make the standby incompatible with the schema, removing the safe switch-back option.
